subdomain: 7.3 Support debugging and operational issue resolution

en.question: An unattended Claude Code run exits successfully after a team changes a permission entry in ordinary project settings, but the intended restriction is absent. Another developer's interactive session behaves differently. Its /status view lists the project settings as loaded. Before changing prompts or permissions, what investigation is most useful?

options.text: Strengthen CLAUDE.md wording first, because a loaded settings source means the remaining difference must be model adherence.
options.note: Listing a settings source does not prove that every value in it was accepted or supplied the effective rule. Rewriting model guidance does not diagnose a dropped or conflicting permission entry.

options.text: Treat /status as per-key provenance and compare model outputs only after ruling out the shared file as a cause.
options.note: /status identifies active settings sources, not the source and validity of each key. It cannot by itself rule out a rejected value or interaction with other applicable settings.

options.text: Use the zero process exit to certify the project settings, then investigate tool-server availability rather than configuration loading.
options.note: A non-interactive run can skip broken ordinary settings or individual values and still continue successfully. Process success therefore does not certify that the intended restriction loaded.

options.text: Record versions and active setting sources, inspect rejected entries with claude doctor, and safely reproduce the restriction using the applicable rules.
options.note: This checks what the client actually accepted and which other sources may affect the outcome. A controlled reproduction verifies the restriction instead of inferring enforcement from a file listing or successful run.
